database: An organized collection of data, stored electronically in a server; typically a computer, computers distributed, or RAID (slide 7). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
RAID: Redundant array of independent disks, to improve robustness or speed (slide 7). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
DBMS|database management system: Manages incoming and outgoing data, organizes it, and provides ways for the data to be modified or extracted by users or other programs; a database is not a DBMS (slides 9, 11). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
persistent: Data in the database outlives the programs that execute on that data (slide 12). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
RDBMS|relational DBMS: A DBMS of related tables that uses the SQL language, such as MySQL, SQLite, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server (slide 14). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
NoSQL: A non-relational DBMS; this course uses only relational DBMSs for its APIs (slide 14). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
SQL: Structured Query Language, the RDBMS language (slide 14). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
CRUD: Create, Read, Update, Delete; the deck's title names it, the expansion is the standard one (slides 1, 14). See [CRUD from Node.js: connect, create, insert, select](#/comp4537-l7/crud-from-node).
1st Normal Form|1NF: Violated by storing multiple values in the same column (slide 16). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
table|entity|relation: Table = Entity = Relation = database object; its name is unique in a database (slides 21-22). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
field|column|attribute: Field = Attribute = Column = variable; a column that keeps one kind of information about every record (slides 21-22). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
record|row|tuple: Record = Row = tuple = instance; each individual entry in a table (slides 21-22). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
cell: Where a data value is stored (slide 22). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
primary key: The column unique to each row, such as Patient_ID in Patient or Visit_ID in Visit (slide 20). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
foreign key: A primary key of another table present in this table, such as Patient_ID in Visit (slide 20). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
one-to-many|1: M: a single row in one table relates to multiple rows of another, as one patient to many visits (slide 23). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
one-to-one|1: 1: each row relates to at most one row of the other table; a patient could visit "only" once (slide 23). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
many-to-many|M: M: modelled as two 1:M relationships through an associative table, as authors and books (slide 66). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
associative entity|associative table: The table, such as authorBook, that links two other tables (slides 68, 70). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
composite primary key: A primary key made of more than one column, such as PRIMARY KEY(authorID, bookID) (slide 67). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
schema: The data model and data types of columns, written with CREATE TABLE (slide 27). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
referential integrity: Rows that refer to another table's row must keep making sense; deleting patient 2 would orphan visits 2 and 3 (slide 30). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
AUTO_INCREMENT: Generates a unique number automatically when a new record is inserted, often for the primary key (slide 71). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
CHECK: Ensures all values in a column satisfy a specific condition, such as Age>=18 (slide 72). See [Tables related by primary and foreign keys](#/comp4537-l7/databases-tables-and-keys).
mysql module: The npm package Node uses to talk to MySQL; external, installed with npm install mysql (L5 slide 43). See [CRUD from Node.js: connect, create, insert, select](#/comp4537-l7/crud-from-node).
createConnection: Mysql.createConnection({host, user, password, database}) creates the connection object, the first of the three steps (L5 slide 44). See [CRUD from Node.js: connect, create, insert, select](#/comp4537-l7/crud-from-node).
InnoDB: The MySQL storage engine Lab 5 names in CREATE TABLE … ENGINE=InnoDB; it enforces foreign keys (Lab 5). See [CRUD from Node.js: connect, create, insert, select](#/comp4537-l7/crud-from-node).
principle of least privilege: Give each DB user only the privileges its job needs, such as a SELECT-only user for reads (Lab 5, slide 13). See [CRUD from Node.js: connect, create, insert, select](#/comp4537-l7/crud-from-node).
cross product|Cartesian product: FROM A, B with no condition pairs every row of A with every row of B, 3 × 3 = 9 rows (slide 26). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
DISTINCT: Keeps unique rows in a result (slide 32). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
LIKE: Searches for a specified pattern in a column inside a WHERE clause (slide 36). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
wildcard: % stands for zero, one or multiple characters, _ for a single character (slides 36-37). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
IN: Specifies multiple values in a WHERE clause; a shorthand for multiple OR conditions (slide 38). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
BETWEEN: Selects values within a range, inclusive of both ends (slide 39). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
ASCII: American Standard Code for Information Interchange; 'A' is 65 and 'a' is 97, so uppercase sorts first (slide 39). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
alias|AS: A name for a result column, as in Quantity*Price AS Total (slide 42). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
aggregate function: A function over values in multiple rows: min, max, sum, avg, count (slides 47, 55). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
GROUP BY: Groups rows that have the same values into summary rows (slide 49). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
HAVING: The filter used after GROUP BY and on aggregate functions, where WHERE cannot be used (slides 55-60). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
subquery: A query inside another, possible because the result of each SQL query is again a table (slide 62). See [Reading the lecture's SQL](#/comp4537-l7/reading-sql).
